messages:
maria: FYI postmortem is in Google Drive, quick sync: we had a repeated 95th-latency spike across the rpc tier during the rollout window. Looking to adjust SLO targets + assign remediation owners. Thoughts?

alex: skimmed the PM, main takeaway is headroom was too tight for the bursty seq lengths. We should avoid global 95th=120ms for the next 30d.

jon: Agree. Also saw cache churn contributing ~12% added p99 latency. That needs followup but separate.

maria: Proposed changes (short):
```
- Temporarily relax user-facing 95th target: 120ms -> 160ms for 30d
- Create a burst-window SLO for peak traffic: 99th inbound latency < 300ms (during 15m spikes)
- Error budget pause: auto-rollout block if burn > 2% per day
```

maria: Proposed owners: Kev for dashboard + alert changes, Tasha for rollout policy update, Jon for cache root cause and KV-cache TTL audit.

kev: I can do dashboards/alerts. I'll add a per-route 95th chart + a spike window panel. ETA EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:

tasha: I'll add an automatic rollback rule in the canary pipeline and a temporary routing policy with fallback to smaller batch sizes. Need an endpoint list from infra.

jon: I'll run the cache TTL sweep and a short test to repro cache churn. Can take 2 days.

alex: We should also capture this as a recurring incident pattern: spikes align with larger sequence inputs from ingestion jobs. File an infra ticket to rate-limit or throttle those jobs.

maria: Agreed. Action items and timelines: Kev (dashboards) - by 2024-06-02; Tasha (rollout policy) - by 2024-06-03; Jon (cache audit) - by 2024-06-04; Alex (ingestion throttling ticket) - by 2024-06-02.

sre-ci-bot: New tasks created: TASK-4821 (Dashboards), TASK-4822 (Canary rollback rule), TASK-4823 (Cache TTL audit), TASK-4824 (Ingestion throttling).

maria: We also need to document the temporary SLO adjustments in the SLO runbook and set a reminder to re-evaluate after 30 days. I'll update the runbook tonight.

kev: Quick question — should the error budget policy be per-service or global for the rpc tier? Per-service gives better signal.

tasha: Per-service sounds safer. We'll set the auto-rollout block at service-level and centralize notifications to #eng-oncall.

jon: One more note: add a dashboard that breaks down latency by sequence length bucket (<256, 256-1024, >1024). That'll help target optimizations.

maria: Good call. I'll mark that as a must-have for Kev's dashboard task.

alex: If anyone sees unexpected burn while the relaxed window is active, @maria please ping to re-open emergency rollback.

maria: Will do. Thanks everyone — can we reconvene in 72h for a quick status check? :eyes:

kev: +1

jon: +1

tasha: +1

alex: +1

maria: Scheduling a 15m check-in in 72h and adding it to the TASKs. Thread closed for now.
